items.title: Map HTTP hops and approve a desync-safe test plan
items.objective: Identify front ends, gateways, protocol versions, downgrade paths, connection reuse, backend affinity, monitoring, and stop conditions before probes.
prerequisites: Written authorization for desynchronization testing and an owner-reviewed proxy topology
An isolated endpoint/window, dedicated test clients, monitoring, and immediate stop/purge capability
steps: Document the exact client-to-edge-to-gateway-to-backend protocol path and normal connection reuse
Send repeated well-formed framing and follow-up controls on a dedicated route
Send one minimal ambiguous-framing/canary pair for the specific variant
Stop immediately on anomalies and require repeatable isolated plus owner-log confirmation

examples.note: No smuggling payload is provided. Build only an owner-reviewed inert canary pair for the confirmed protocol path.

items.manipulate: One message-framing, downgrade, normalization, timeout, or connection-reuse condition at a time on an isolated path
items.secure_behavior: Every hop rejects ambiguous framing or derives the same boundary; protocol downgrade creates canonical messages and closes safely after errors.
items.vulnerable_behavior: the owner cannot establish a safe isolated route/window or identify shared-user impact controls, so runtime testing remains blocked
items.validation: Require repeatable paired controls, same-path connection evidence, and isolated owner-assisted confirmation; a timeout, rejection difference, or one odd response is insufficient.
false_positives: external observations can leave some internal hops uncertain
a single-origin deployment can still use several managed proxy layers
items.impact: Confirmed desynchronization can poison request/response queues, bypass front-end controls, capture another user’s response, poison caches, or route attacker-controlled prefixes into victim requests.
evidence: Approved hop/protocol topology and isolated test route
Exact raw bytes/frames for baseline and one canary pair
Connection, backend affinity, timestamps, and owner proxy logs
Repeatable assessor-only effect, stop conditions, and proof no shared traffic was affected

Send one minimal ambiguous-framing/canary pair for the specific variant
Stop immediately on anomalies and require repeatable isolated plus owner-log confirmation

examples.note: No smuggling payload is provided. Build only an owner-reviewed inert canary pair for the confirmed protocol path.

items.manipulate: One message-framing, downgrade, normalization, timeout, or connection-reuse condition at a time on an isolated path
items.secure_behavior: Every hop rejects ambiguous framing or derives the same boundary; protocol downgrade creates canonical messages and closes safely after errors.
items.vulnerable_behavior: a previously confirmed isolated canary still crosses a boundary or another protocol path remains inconsistent
items.validation: Require repeatable paired controls, same-path connection evidence, and isolated owner-assisted confirmation; a timeout, rejection difference, or one odd response is insufficient.
false_positives: a changed rejection status can be secure if no bytes reach downstream
different routes can intentionally use separate proxy stacks
items.impact: Confirmed desynchronization can poison request/response queues, bypass front-end controls, capture another user’s response, poison caches, or route attacker-controlled prefixes into victim requests.
evidence: Approved hop/protocol topology and isolated test route
Exact raw bytes/frames for baseline and one canary pair
Connection, backend affinity, timestamps, and owner proxy logs
Repeatable assessor-only effect, stop conditions, and proof no shared traffic was affected
tools: HTTP Request Smuggler in manual safe mode

references.title: WSTG v4.2: Testing for HTTP Splitting and Smuggling

items.safety: REVIEW ONLY. Obtain explicit owner approval, prefer an isolated environment and dedicated route, send one paired canary probe at a time, never target shared-user traffic, and stop on any queue, latency, error-rate, or unexpected-response anomaly.
items.remediation: Reject conflicting/ambiguous framing at the first hop, align patched parsers, canonicalize HTTP/2/3 downgrade, avoid forwarding forbidden fields, close connections on errors, and test every route/protocol path.
